acceptance.given: Package A validator tests and required fixtures/selectors are authored in the declared scripts/sc/tests scope, with the production validator entry available.

oracle.expected: Executing the selected tests invokes the real validate_package entry or published CLI and compares structured status, rule IDs, diagnostic path and code, plus applicable boundary effects; replacing the validator with an unconditional pass causes the tests to fail.
forbidden: Tests rely only on mocks instead of the real validator entry or CLI.
Any named structured result field or relevant boundary effect is not compared.
oracle.observable: Test assertions and subprocess invocation records show real validator execution and explicit comparisons for status, rule IDs, path, code, and applicable boundary effects.

acceptance.then: The test oracle demonstrates real-entry validation coverage for the required structured outputs and rejects an unconditional-pass validator.
acceptance.when: Run the Package A validator test command; during evaluation inspect the test call path, parsed result assertions, and mutation or boundary case outcomes.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A declared Package A pytest case invokes scripts/sc/validate_skill_quality.py::validate_package or the published CLI with literal argv and fails by AssertionError when structured status, rule IDs, path, code, or applicable boundary effects are not compared.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or repair Package A tests so they exercise the real validator entry or CLI and assert the complete structured result and relevant boundary effects.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Tests remain compatible with the versioned validator result schema and do not alter persisted state or schemas.

slice_hint.state_transition: Package A test oracles transition from authored intent to executable real-entry structured assertions.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted Package A pytest selector and terminal four-module command execute the real validator, compare status, rule IDs, path, code and boundary effects, and fail on an unconditional-pass replacement.
